jess_customer: Hey support — since the 10:11 deploy we're intermittently getting invalid JSON from /v1/generate in JSON mode. Client parser fails with 'Unexpected token' and we see multiple JSON objects concatenated or duplicated keys. Example attached.

maria_support: Thanks — can you paste the raw response and a x-request-id? Also are you using batching or our kv cache? :eyes:

jess_customer: x-request-id: req-20260315-8f2b
Raw response:
```
{\"choices\":[{\"text\":\"{\\\"id\\\":1, \\\"name\\\":\\\"alice\\\"}\"}],\"meta\":{}}
{\"choices\":[{\"text\":\"{\\\"id\\\":2, \\\"name\\\":\\\"bob\\\"}\"}],\"meta\":{}}
```
Notice it's two JSON objects with no separator — client can't parse.

ops-bot: deploy: rollout v1.13 -> runtime:inference (started at 2026-03-15T10:11:58Z) :information_source:

eli_engineer: assigning to eng-runtime. Can you repro with `debug=true` and send headers? I want `x-kv-shard`, `x-request-id`, `x-client-batch`.

jess_customer: sending header dump:
`x-request-id: req-20260315-8f2b`
`x-kv-shard: 42`
`x-client-batch: true`
Also note we use batch_size=8 and KV_CACHE=enabled.

maria_support: escalating to eng-sre. tagging @ana_sre :fire_engine:

ana_sre: I'll check routing logs. We've seen a rare shard-handoff race when batching + kv cache prefetch overlap. Can you also provide timeline and any matching `shard_seq` if present?

jess_customer: timeline: first failure 2026-03-15T10:12:05Z, then ~every ~30s for ~10 minutes. No shard_seq from client side.

eli_engineer: pulled internal logs for req-20260315-8f2b:
```
[10:12:04.998] write_shard: shard=42 -> worker=17 seq=100 payload_len=1024 checksum=0x9a7f
[10:12:05.001] write_shard: shard=17 -> worker=17 seq=101 payload_len=512 checksum=0x4b2a
[10:12:05.002] combine_streams: got payload from shard=42 then shard=17 without separator
```
Looks like handoff ordering got mixed and the stream concatenated two JSON documents with no delimiter. Root cause hypothesis: concurrent handoff path doesn't insert boundary markers when batch coalescing occurs.

ana_sre: bingo. There's a known window where `handoff_in_flight` and `prefetch_write` can interleave if `kv_prefetch=true` and `batch_coalesce` is enabled. Need handshake including `shard_id` and a boundary token.

maria_support: Proposed immediate mitigations for customer: 1) set `x-client-batch:false` (client-side batching off) or 2) disable KV_CACHE (set KV_CACHE=off) or 3) set `batch_size=1` on request. Which do you want us to try now?

jess_customer: we'll disable client batching and KV cache temporarily. Also worried about charges — we retried a bunch before contacting you. Can billing review the token usage window 10:11:58-10:25:00?

billing_team: Hi — we'll mark that window as service disruption and waive token charges for retries that match `req-20260315-*`. Please send the list of request ids and rough TTL.

eli_engineer: short term patch: add explicit `--boundary:0x1E` (RS char) into the stream encoder between shard writes and add a handshake check (shard checksum). Long term: fix coalescer lock ordering and add unit test. I'll open PR and schedule canary.

ana_sre: I'll run a targeted canary in prod with handshake enforced and monitor for reoccurrence. Also generating alerts for "unexpected concatenated json" metric.

maria_support: Customer update sent. Action items: (1) eng-runtime to PR + canary (eli) (2) SRE to run canary + alerts (ana) (3) Support to follow up and confirm billing waiver (maria). Jess — we'll ping when patch is canaried.

jess_customer: thanks — workaround reduced failures immediately. Please keep me posted, we depend on structured output for ingestion pipelines.

maria_support: noted. I'll close the loop after canary. :white_check_mark:
